name: MGX Fund Management Limited (MGX Group Holding 1 Ltd)
headquarters: Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates — 13th Floor, Al Sarab Tower, Abu Dhabi Global Market Square, Al Maryah Island (ADGM); US arm MGX Fund Management (US) LLC at 50 Hudson Yards, New York
employees: Not stated on any MGX channel; the leadership page names 10 executives and the ADGM register lists 12 approved persons. Collection gap.
summary:
BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: MGX is Abu Dhabi's state-backed AI investment vehicle — created in March 2024 by the Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council with Mubadala and G42 as 'foundational partners', chaired by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed — and in fourteen months it has become the largest single pool of dedicated AI capital on the record: MGX Fund I closed on 1 July 2026 at USD 49 billion against a USD 45 billion target with 14 portfolio companies, it is one of four initial equity funders of Stargate LLC, a co-founder of the AI Infrastructure Partnership (AIP) with BlackRock, GIP and Microsoft, and, with AIP and GIP, the owner since 21 July 2026 of Aligned Data Centers (about USD 40 billion enterprise value, 51 campuses, 6.4 GW). Its relevance to this corpus is that it now sits behind the money in ten dossiers — OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI as a repeat investor, Aligned and Vantage as an owner — while publishing no ticket sizes, no stake percentages, no AUM total and no headcount.

BACKGROUND. Legal structure per MGX's own footer: MGX Group Holding 1 Ltd (ADGM) owns MGX Fund Management Limited, licensed by the ADGM Financial Services Regulatory Authority on 18 October 2024 (FSP 240067) to manage collective investment funds and, from June 2025, to advise on and arrange investments; four funds are registered (MGX Fund I LP, an AIV and two co-investment vehicles). Board: Chairman Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan (UAE National Security Advisor, chairman of G42, ADIA, ADQ, IHC and FAB), Vice Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak (Mubadala Group CEO), Jassem Al Zaabi, Peng Xiao (G42 Group CEO) and Martin Edelman; Managing Director and CEO Ahmed Yahia Al Idrissi (formerly CEO of Mubadala's direct investments platform, ex-McKinsey partner) also chairs the Investment Committee and is Vice Chairman of AIP. Three stated pillars: semiconductors, AI digital infrastructure, AI technology; about 70% of capital to North America. Named holdings (portfolio page, 13): AIP, Aligned, Altera, Anthropic, Binance, Campus AI, Databricks, Isomorphic Labs, Khazna, OpenAI, SpaceX (xAI after the merger), TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC and Vantage Data Centers. Disclosed amounts are few: USD 2 billion for a minority stake in Binance (March 2025, settled in World Liberty Financial's USD1 stablecoin), 15% of the TikTok USDS JV (January 2026), co-lead of Anthropic's USD 30 billion Series G and of OpenAI's USD 122 billion round (2026), participation in xAI's USD 20 billion Series E, and a reported (Bloomberg) about USD 7 billion Stargate commitment that no principal has confirmed. The board stated in May 2026 that portfolio companies' contracted AI-infrastructure capacity is 'projected to exceed 8GWs by the end of 2026'.
ecosystemRole: The sovereign capital behind the largest AI build-outs this corpus tracks: an initial equity funder of Stargate LLC (with SoftBank, OpenAI and Oracle), co-founder and Vice Chair seat-holder of the AI Infrastructure Partnership whose first investment was Aligned Data Centers, an owner in Vantage Data Centers 'to support the Stargate build-out of 2.3 gigawatts in Texas and Wisconsin', a repeat investor in OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI, and — through AIP's agreements with GE Vernova and NextEra Energy — a stated backer of 'all forms of energy' for AI data centres. MGX owns no power project and has no energy strategy of its own; every energy statement on its channels is made through AIP, Aligned or Campus AI.

productsAndServices.name: MGX Fund I — the USD 49 billion AI fund
productsAndServices.description: MGX's flagship closed-end vehicle, registered in ADGM as MGX Fund I LP (established 8 May 2024) with an alternative investment vehicle (AIV-1, July 2025) and two co-investment partnerships (August 2025). Final close confirmed 1 July 2026 at 'USD 49 billion in total commitments, significantly above its initial $45 billion target fund size' from 'major institutional and private investors from the Gulf, North America, Asia and Europe'; 'Since inception, MGX Fund I has invested in 14 companies'. Strategy: 'highly curated exposure to the AI thematic through disciplined investments in differentiated and restricted opportunities across the AI technology stack, including semiconductors, AI infrastructure and AI and AI-enabling technologies and platforms'.
highlights: USD 49 billion final close vs USD 45 billion target (1 July 2026); press calls it the largest dedicated AI fund raised to date; equivalent AED 180 billion (Khaleej Times).

14 portfolio companies since inception; the portfolio page names 13 (AIP, Aligned, Altera, Anthropic, Binance, Campus AI, Databricks, Isomorphic Labs, Khazna, OpenAI, SpaceX, TikTok USDS JV, Vantage) — one holding is unnamed.

No LP is named by MGX or any outlet; the Mubadala and G42 contributions are undisclosed. Bloomberg (January 2025) recorded a founding target of 'eventual assets of $100 billion'; press cites a deployment pace of about USD 10 billion a year (Quartz, PYMNTS, Semafor).

Regulated entity: MGX Fund Management Limited, FSP 240067, 'Managing a Collective Investment Fund' (18 October 2024), 'Advising on Investments or Credit' and 'Arranging Deals in Investments' (23 June 2025); Qualified Investor Funds only — 'not permitted to deal with Retail Clients'.
Geography: 'Approximately 70% of our capital is allocated to North America with the remainder across the UAE, Western Europe and selected APAC countries'.
productsAndServices.positioning: Larger than any single AI-dedicated private vehicle on the record and sovereign-backed, MGX's stated differentiator is access — 'differentiated and restricted opportunities' — through its chairman's and Mubadala's relationships (Semafor's 'playbook' account) and co-investment with Silver Lake, BlackRock/GIP, SoftBank and Bpifrance. Comparable pools of AI-infrastructure capital in the corpus are AIP itself (USD 30 billion equity / USD 100 billion with debt), Brookfield's and Blackstone's infrastructure funds, and SoftBank's Vision Funds; none is a state AI champion in the way MGX describes itself.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct commitments from institutional and private LPs; ADGM Qualified Investor Fund structures; co-investment vehicles for deal-level partners.
targetSegments: Gulf, North American, Asian and European institutional and private investors (LPs)
AI companies and platforms seeking a sovereign anchor investor with US, UAE and European reach
productsAndServices.roadmap: Board releases in February 2026 noted 'strong fundraising momentum, including new commitments from top-tier international investors'; no successor fund has been announced.

productsAndServices.name: AI Infrastructure Partnership (AIP) and Aligned Data Centers
productsAndServices.description: AIP (launched 17 September 2024 as the Global AI Infrastructure Investment Partnership by BlackRock, Global Infrastructure Partners, Microsoft and MGX, with NVIDIA as technical partner) seeks 'to unlock $30 billion of private equity capital over time' and 'up to $100 billion in total investment potential when including debt financing' for data centres and 'energy infrastructure to create new sources of power for these facilities', chiefly in the United States. NVIDIA and xAI joined in March 2025, Cisco as technology partner, Kuwait Investment Authority (June 2025) and Temasek as financial anchors; GE Vernova and NextEra Energy 'agreed to collaborate with AIP to accelerate the scaling of critical and diverse energy solutions for AI data centers'. AIP's first investment — with MGX and GIP as direct co-buyers — was Aligned Data Centers: 100% of the equity from Macquarie Asset Management funds at about USD 40 billion enterprise value, announced 15 October 2025 and closed 21 July 2026 with 'an additional $5 billion of growth capital' committed.
highlights: Aligned at close: '51 campuses and more than 6.4GW of operational and planned capacity' across Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas, Ohio, Phoenix, Salt Lake City, São Paulo, Querétaro and Santiago; CEO Andrew Schaap and team retained; HQ Dallas.
Governance seats: Ahmed Yahia Al Idrissi is Vice Chairman of AIP; Andre Namphy (MGX CLO) sits on AIP's Investment Committee; David Scott sits on AIP's board.

MGX's percentage of Aligned, the consortium's debt package and AIP's committed capital to date are undisclosed. ESG Dive lists AIP's members as BlackRock, Microsoft, NVIDIA, xAI, Temasek and KIA with Cisco as technology partner.

Energy: NextEra's CEO in the March 2025 release — 'an all forms of energy solution that leverages ready-now renewables and battery storage coupled with gas-fired and nuclear generation'; GE Vernova to 'work with AIP and its partners on supply chain planning'. Aligned's own October 2025 release adds a 31 MW / 62 MWh Calibrant battery in the Pacific Northwest.
Reported, not confirmed: Bloomberg-sourced reports (June 2026, in this corpus's STACK Infrastructure dossier) name the BlackRock/Microsoft/MGX-backed AIP among suitors for STACK's APAC portfolio.
productsAndServices.positioning: AIP is the vehicle through which MGX competes with Brookfield, Blackstone/QTS, DigitalBridge and KKR for hyperscale landlords; Aligned's 6.4 GW makes the consortium one of the largest owners of US data-centre capacity after one transaction. The energy leg — GE Vernova and NextEra agreements — is the part of MGX's footprint that touches this corpus's power and storage suppliers.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Platform equity through AIP alongside direct co-investment (MGX and GIP were named buyers of Aligned separately from AIP).
targetSegments: Hyperscale and AI data-centre operators (Aligned's tenants)
Power and energy-infrastructure counterparties via the GE Vernova and NextEra collaborations
productsAndServices.roadmap: AIP's stated focus is 'the U.S. as well as OECD and U.S. partner countries'; USD 5 billion of growth capital committed to Aligned at closing; no second AIP investment announced as of September 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Frontier models and core AI — OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI/SpaceX, Databricks, Isomorphic Labs
productsAndServices.description: MGX's repeat positions in the frontier labs and data platforms this corpus tracks as compute buyers. OpenAI: participant in the October 2024 round (amount undisclosed), 'an additional major investment ... in its most recent $300 billion valuation funding round' (2025), a fourth follow-on via the employee secondary, and 'co-lead in OpenAI's latest US$122 billion funding round' at USD 852 billion (March 2026) — 'MGX's fifth follow-on in OpenAI'. Anthropic: first backed by May 2025, co-lead of the USD 30 billion Series G at USD 380 billion post-money (February 2026) and a 'significant investor' in the USD 65 billion Series H at USD 965 billion (May 2026). xAI: Series C (December 2024) and USD 20 billion Series E (January 2026), then the SpaceX merger. Databricks: co-lead of the USD 1 billion Series K (September 2025), Series L at USD 134 billion (December 2025) and the USD 5 billion round at USD 190 billion (August 2026); new investor in the USD 10 billion Series J (December 2024). Isomorphic Labs: new investor in the USD 2.1 billion Series B (May 2026), 'MGX's first foray' into AI drug discovery.
highlights: No dollar amount or stake is disclosed for any of these positions; MGX declined to give its OpenAI ticket to AGBI (October 2024). Anthropic lists MGX as a co-lead in Series G alongside D. E. Shaw Ventures, Dragoneer, Founders Fund and ICONIQ (GIC and Coatue led).

Anthropic's acceptance of Gulf capital is documented as contested internally: WIRED (via Fwdstart) quoted Dario Amodei's 2025 memo — 'This is a real downside and I'm not thrilled about it' — with any deal to be 'narrowly scoped, purely financial' and without governance rights; The Intercept (June 2026) reports MGX in both Series G and H.

xAI names MGX among Series E investors with Valor, StepStone, Fidelity, QIA and Baron; MGX's own X post: 'This investment supports the rapid scaling of compute infrastructure and the buildout of the largest GPU clusters in the world.'
OpenAI is also MGX's Stargate co-funder; the board's December 2025 release describes 'deepening partnerships with leading AI shapers, such as OpenAI, xAI and Databricks'.
productsAndServices.positioning: Among sovereign and quasi-sovereign AI investors (QIA, GIC, Temasek, PIF vehicles), MGX is the only one that is simultaneously a co-lead in OpenAI and Anthropic rounds, a Stargate equity funder and an owner of the landlords (Aligned, Vantage) those labs lease from — the layered-counterparty pattern this corpus's Anthropic and OpenAI dossiers describe.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Minority primary and secondary equity in private rounds, typically alongside a US lead investor.
targetSegments: Data and AI platforms (Databricks) and AI-enabled life sciences (Isomorphic Labs)
productsAndServices.roadmap: MGX's board language commits to 'frontier models and platforms to the infrastructure required to scale them globally'; no exit, listing or secondary sale of any position has been announced.

productsAndServices.name: Compute campuses and colocation — Stargate LLC, Vantage, Khazna, Campus AI (France)
productsAndServices.description: Stargate LLC: SoftBank's 22 January 2025 release names 'SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle, and MGX' as 'the initial equity funders' of the USD 500 billion, four-year programme (SoftBank financial responsibility, OpenAI operational); Bloomberg reported MGX 'is contributing approximately $7 billion', which no principal has confirmed, and MGX's own channels carry no Stargate release. Vantage Data Centers (North America): 'further investments in Vantage Data Centers to support the Stargate build-out of 2.3 gigawatts in Texas and Wisconsin' (board release, December 2025). Khazna Data Centers: minority stake alongside Silver Lake with G42 as majority owner (March 2025), described by the board as MGX's route into Stargate UAE. Campus AI: joint venture with Bpifrance, Mistral AI and NVIDIA for a 1.4 GW Paris-region campus (May 2025; construction from H2 2026, operations by 2028; EDF and RTE as partners), expanded in June 2026 toward 'up to 3 GW of compute capacity nationwide' with a second site.
highlights: Stargate caveats: SoftBank's September 2025 five-new-sites release names only OpenAI, Oracle and SoftBank; Stargate UAE's releases (G42, OpenAI, Oracle, NVIDIA, SoftBank, Cisco) do not name MGX; The Information (via The Decoder, February 2026) reports the JV 'hasn't hired any staff'. MGX is a committed initial funder of a vehicle whose operating form is disputed in the press.

The Information (via TechCrunch) framed the Stargate split as OpenAI and SoftBank at USD 19 billion each for 40% each with Oracle and MGX in the remaining 20% — a combined figure that conflicts with Bloomberg's about USD 7 billion for MGX alone; both are recorded as reported.
Vantage: amount undisclosed; the corpus's Vantage dossier carries the Texas (Frontier) and Wisconsin (Lighthouse) Stargate campuses.
Campus AI: Bloomberg put the first phase at EUR 8.5 billion (RCR Wireless); AGBI reports a EUR 7.5 billion June 2026 expansion partnership; equity split undisclosed.
Khazna: e& sold its 40% to G42 for AED 8 billion (AGBI); MGX's and Silver Lake's stakes are undisclosed.
productsAndServices.positioning: MGX holds the campus layer on both sides of the Atlantic: Stargate and Vantage in the US, Khazna in the UAE, Campus AI in France — the physical footprint behind the '8GWs by the end of 2026' contracted-capacity statement, though that figure is MGX's own and is not broken down.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: JV equity (Stargate LLC, Campus AI), platform equity (Vantage), minority stakes (Khazna).
targetSegments: Hyperscaler and frontier-lab compute tenants (OpenAI at Stargate; Mistral at Campus AI)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Campus AI construction 'expected to begin in the second half of 2026, with operations launching by 2028'; Stargate UAE's first 200 MW in 2026 (G42); no dated MGX-specific milestone.

productsAndServices.name: Semiconductors and strategic platforms — Altera, TikTok USDS JV, Binance
productsAndServices.description: Altera: co-investor with Silver Lake in the acquisition of a 51% stake from Intel (which retains 49%) 'valuing the company at $8.7 billion and establishing the world's largest independent pure-play FPGA business' (September 2025). TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC: one of three managing investors — Silver Lake, Oracle and MGX 'each holding 15%' — with ByteDance at 19.9% (January 2026); David Scott sits on the seven-member board and its security committee. Binance: 'a landmark $2 billion investment ... the first institutional investment in Binance', a minority stake and 'the single largest investment into a crypto company and the largest investment ever paid in crypto (stablecoin)' (March 2025), settled in World Liberty Financial's USD1.
highlights: Altera cheque size undisclosed; Omar Alismail (CIO Semiconductors & Infrastructure): 'Altera provides a foundational platform for next generation computing.'
TikTok USDS: dollar amount undisclosed; Semafor put the US app's valuation at USD 14 billion; the venture is the only MGX holding with a stated percentage other than Binance's 'minority'.

Binance/USD1: the settlement stablecoin belongs to the Trump-family-linked World Liberty Financial; Reuters, ABC and WSJ-sourced reporting document the controversy, Binance's CEO said the USD1 choice 'was made by MGX', and Senators Warren and Merkley wrote to MGX and Binance. Recorded as reported context, not as an MGX statement.
productsAndServices.positioning: These are access-driven stakes rather than a thesis: Altera through Silver Lake, TikTok through the US divestiture process, Binance as a first crypto position. The semiconductors pillar is otherwise unfilled on the portfolio page — no foundry, memory or GPU position is named despite the pillar's prominence in MGX's strategy.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Consortium minority equity alongside Silver Lake and Oracle; direct minority investment (Binance).
targetSegments: Semiconductor platforms (FPGA), US-regulated technology divestitures, digital-asset exchanges

relationships.context:
MGX's board releases record the sequence: participation in the October 2024 round (amount undisclosed), 'an additional major investment in OpenAI in its most recent $300 billion valuation funding round' (September 2025), 'participation in OpenAI's latest employee secondary—its fourth follow-on investment in OpenAI' (February 2026) and 'participation as co-lead in OpenAI's latest US$122 billion funding round. policyExposure.regime: US export controls — UAE chip access (Country Group A:5, July 2026)
policyExposure.exposure: MGX's US and UAE portfolio depends on advanced-chip flows that were restricted under the Biden-era proposals and G42's prior Commerce scrutiny (Bloomberg, January 2025; House and Senate Democrats, May 2025). In July 2026 Commerce moved the UAE to Country Group A:5 — licence-free shipment of certain sensitive technologies — and, per CNBC via Incrypted, 'said it would view favorably export applications for semiconductors and server equipment destined for MGX'; Senator Warren's 10 July statement describes 'favorable treatment for MGX' and links it to a UAE-linked stake in World Liberty Financial, calling for Commerce testimony.
policyExposure.mitigation: None stated by MGX. MGX did not respond to The Intercept; its channels carry no export-control statement.

policyExposure.mitigation: None stated by MGX; the Binance release describes the deal only as 'the largest investment ever paid in crypto (stablecoin)'.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that MGX is a state AI champion operating as a fund, and that its edge is access rather than analysis. Basis: created by a government council with the UAE's National Security Advisor as chairman and the Mubadala and G42 chiefs on its board; the 'differentiated and restricted opportunities' language in its own fund-close release; co-lead roles in OpenAI and Anthropic rounds within two years of formation; Semafor's account of a 'playbook' built on leadership relationships and co-investment with Silver Lake, BlackRock/GIP and SoftBank. The USD 49 billion close from unnamed Gulf, North American, Asian and European LPs shows third-party capital has followed.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that MGX's exposure to this corpus runs through ownership of the landlords and the labs at once, and that no MGX statement quantifies either. Basis: initial equity funder of Stargate LLC (SoftBank release), owner of Aligned (about USD 40 billion EV, 6.4 GW) with AIP and GIP, investor in Vantage 'to support the Stargate build-out of 2.3 gigawatts', and repeat investor in OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI — while every ticket, stake and the Stargate contribution are undisclosed (Bloomberg's about USD 7 billion is press-reported). The '8GWs by the end of 2026' contracted-capacity figure is MGX's own aggregate.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that Stargate LLC is a smaller part of MGX's actual footprint than its ten corpus mentions imply. Basis: MGX has never issued a Stargate release; SoftBank's September 2025 expansion and every Stargate UAE release omit MGX; The Information (February 2026) reports the JV never hired staff and that OpenAI works bilaterally with Oracle. MGX's dated, first-party Stargate exposure is via Vantage and Khazna — landlords — rather than the JV. A confirmed MGX equity contribution to Stargate LLC would reverse this judgment.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that US political risk to MGX has moved from background to foreground in 2026 and is now the main threat to its North American deployment. Basis: the Binance settlement in the Trump-family-linked USD1 stablecoin (May 2025) drew Senate letters; the July 2026 export-control relaxation for the UAE, with Commerce's stated favourable view of applications 'destined for MGX', drew Senator Warren's calls for testimony and a CNBC-reported USD 500 million UAE-linked stake in World Liberty Financial; Anthropic's own memo treats Gulf capital as 'a real downside'. About 70% of MGX's capital is allocated to North America, so an adverse turn in Congress or a change of administration bears directly on the book.

5. **(Low confidence)** We assess that MGX's energy exposure is entirely derivative and that no MGX-owned power asset should be expected. Basis: every energy statement on MGX channels is made through AIP (GE Vernova and NextEra 'all forms of energy' collaborations), Aligned (cooling efficiency, a 31 MW / 62 MWh Calibrant battery) or Campus AI (EDF, RTE); David Scott's ENEC and TerraPower board seats are personal. A direct MGX investment in generation, fuel or storage would move this judgment; none is announced.

Collection gap: no headcount; no Mubadala or G42 ownership percentage (a 'ownership-v3.jpg' graphic on the site could not be read); no LP names; no ticket or stake for any frontier-lab, Aligned, Vantage, Khazna, Altera or Stargate position; the mgx.ae news index shows a '$18B Series K' headline for Databricks where the X post and board release say USD 1 billion (treated as a site typo); no MGX statement on the 18–19 May 2026 change of licensed directors at the regulated entity; the alleged intelligence findings on G42 and the reported G42 US-redomiciling plan were not verifiable from any fetched page. Premise check against the coverage-plan row: 'Stargate and Aligned money (10 dossiers)' holds for Aligned (owner since 21 July 2026) and holds narrowly for Stargate (named initial equity funder; contribution unconfirmed; later Stargate communications omit MGX); two of the ten corpus MGX mentions turned out to be NVIDIA's MGX rack architecture, not the fund — see the step 7 note in the session record.

INDICATORS TO WATCH — *Q4 2026 — AIP's second investment:* a power, chip or campus asset would show whether AIP is a data-centre owner or a broader infrastructure platform; *end-2026 — the '8 GW' contracted-capacity claim:* any breakdown by asset would make Judgment 2 testable; *2026–2027 — a first-party Stargate LLC statement naming MGX's contribution:* would reverse Judgment 3; *congressional action on UAE chip access or the USD1 matter:* hearings or legislation naming MGX would confirm Judgment 4; *any MGX investment in generation, fuel or storage:* would end Judgment 5; *a successor fund announcement:* the first test of whether the USD 49 billion close is repeatable.
